summary: A 12x12 ft lookout cabin on Mineral Mountain, built 1929; lookout men 1928-1929; removed or destroyed in the 1940s; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in the 1940s, according to the sources; no source describes what remains.

events.note: Fred Dahl transferred to Mineral Mountain as lookout man, per the Republic News-Miner (June 29, 1928); willhite says there was a lookout camp in 1928
Several fires in deserted ranch buildings near Boyds, discovered by the Mineral Mountain lookout and controlled by two rangers (July 1928)
12x12 ft cabin built; lumber packed in by horse over a six-mile trail; Mike Moran completing the building by October 1929
J. Williams of Kettle Falls named as the 1929 lookout
Sources say removed (firetower.org) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in the 1940s; 1940 is the start of that decade, not a dated record

evidence.supports: Cabin was 12x12 ft, built 1929, and removed in the 1940s
evidence.quote: This 12'x12' cabin, built in 1929, was removed in the 1940s.

evidence.supports: Cabin built 1929 and destroyed in the 1940s per firelookout.com; J. Williams the 1929 lookout
evidence.quote: This 12x12' cabin, built in 1929, was destroyed in the 1940's. Known lookout personnel: 1929: J. Williams.

evidence.supports: Lookout house to overlook the Columbia River from Marcus to Northport (1929)
evidence.quote: Lloyd Hougland left Tuesday for Orient where he will assist in the construction of a lookout house on Mineral mountain. This is a new lookout point which overlooks the lower country along the Columbia River from Marcus to Northport.

evidence.supports: Lumber packed in by horse over a six-mile trail, by two men
evidence.quote: Ed Smith of Orient and Bud Williams of Kettle Falls are packing the Mineral Mountain Lookout. This lumber is packed full lengths with horses in tandem over a rough trail 6 miles in length.

evidence.supports: Mike Moran completing the building by October 1929
evidence.quote: Mike Moran is completing the Lookout building on Mineral mountain.

evidence.supports: Fred Dahl transferred to Mineral Mountain as lookout man in June 1928
evidence.quote: Fred Dahl who had been doing maintenance work at First Thought lookout is transferred to Mineral mountain as lookout man.

evidence.supports: A lookout camp existed on Mineral Mountain in 1928
evidence.quote: In 1928, Mineral Mountain had a lookout camp.

evidence.supports: Fires near Boyds in deserted ranch buildings, discovered by the lookout and controlled by two rangers
evidence.quote: Several fires were started in the vicinity of Boyds last week, in deserted ranch buildings. The fires were discovered by Mineral Mt. Lookout and controlled by Rangers Duffield and Vincent.

evidence.supports: J. Williams named as the 1929 lookout
evidence.quote: J. Williams of Kettle Falls will be the lookout on Mineral Mountain.

evidence.supports: Cabin removed or destroyed in the 1940s, with no finer distinction
evidence.quote: In the 1940s, the building was removed or destroyed.

evidence.supports: A National Geodetic Survey listing still carries the lookout house name; entry gives no condition
Site lies in Stevens County within the Colville National Forest
The NGS entry also gives a 1992 USGS map name and no description of the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says removed in the 1940s, firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1940s, and WillhiteWeb says removed or destroyed. The story gives the shared 1940s date and reports that the sources disagree on how the cabin ended.

sources.title: Mineral Mountain - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (washingtonlookouts.weebly.com), quoting the Republic News-Miner and the Colville Examiner

notes_for_editor: Only four lookout histories were read, plus no Forest Service record. No source describes the site today and no access source was found, so access is left out. The brief's 2012 FFLOS registration date is not in the story. The NGS entry was read only as reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the datasheet for PID TP0913 was not opened, and it could show whether a survey mark stands on the summit. Fate is disputed between sources and the story says so.
